answers.ask: No theme was stated - should the world below read as high fantasy, or something else?
answers.answer: Use a simple high-fantasy environment below the course, fitting the dragon flight premise.

answers.ask: How many rings should the course have? The HUD example implies ten.
answers.answer: Use 10 rings, as implied by the HUD example.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D dragon flight-racing map with a sequential aerial course of 10 large floating rings, each clearly numbered and arranged as a continuous route through the sky. Frame the course from a third-person view behind and slightly above the flying dragon. Below the course, build a simple high-fantasy landscape with varied terrain forming a visible ground layer beneath the open air route.
agent_notes: Self-declared as racing, and it is a timed course run once from a start to a final gate, which is route-point-to-point rather than a lap circuit. I took Swimming Lanes because it is the one preset that builds a volumetric corridor course — volume-open is how the doc expresses flight, and the ten numbered rings are the flight equivalent of lane markings — dropping its path-turnaround since nothing reverses direction, and adding startpoint-line, per-ring split detection, and hazard-kill for the stated crash-into-terrain loss. P6 is genre-wide and the ring order has to be one followable route; CHECK rides along with the open flight volume, and it should resolve without P2 because the course is a single play-height envelope over one continuous landscape rather than a self-occluding stack. Decided without a user: 10 rings and a plain high-fantasy landscape below per the answers, and the HUD timer and ring counter are interface, so they carry no layout picks beyond the finish trigger.
